title: Compare smaller local models with the outside model for nightly categorisation
description:
## What changes for the user
Every night, the transactions that fixed rules cannot classify are sent to an outside provider's
model: their descriptions, amounts and counterpart names leave the home server, and each call is
billed. The user accepted that for now and asked to know whether a smaller model running at home
could do the same job. Once this lands they have that answer in numbers taken from their own
transactions: which home-run model came closest, how far it trails or beats the outside one, and
whether switching would mean correcting more transactions by hand.

## Outcome
A committed report compares at least three models that run on the user's own hardware against the
outside model on the same set of transactions the user has already confirmed or corrected, and
ends with one recommendation: switch, keep the outside model, or send only the uncertain rows
outside.

## Context
The app assigns each transaction to a budget line, which is one row of the user's monthly budget
(groceries, transport and so on). Fixed rules do most of it: a company that always lands on the
same line is mapped once. What the rules cannot place goes to a language model in a nightly job
that runs with nobody present. The model's answer is applied by itself only when its confidence
is at or above a threshold the user sets, called the auto-apply threshold here; below it the
transaction waits in a queue for the user to decide.

It was decided that the backend reaches the model by calling an HTTP API directly, in the chat
format that outside providers and local model runtimes both accept, so that changing model is a
matter of two configuration values, the base URL and the model name. This bead is the test of
that claim as much as of the models: if a local model needs a different request, the claim is
false and the report must say so.

The user's words when asking for this: outside providers are fine "por enquanto", with a bead to
"avaliar/testar modelos locais menores". Privacy is one reason and cost the other. One guard
already holds on every path: a personal tax number (CPF) is never part of a request, because it
does not help classification.

Two constraints shape the work and are easy to break by accident:

- **The repository is public and the evaluation set is real financial data.** The labelled set
  and every per-row output stay outside the repository, in a directory git ignores. The report
  publishes aggregates only: no description, no counterpart name, no amount per row. Test
  fixtures are synthetic.
- **Which models to try is decided when the work runs, not here.** The set of small models that
  are worth trying changes from month to month, so naming them now would date the bead. The
  criteria fix how many and how they are compared instead.

The evaluation tool may be a script outside the backend, in Python, since it is run by hand a few
times and never deployed. The user was told this and did not object. It must send the same
request the nightly job sends, which is why this bead cannot start before that job exists.

It cannot start yet for a second reason: there is nothing to evaluate against until the user has
used the app long enough to confirm or correct a few hundred categorisations. Both waits are on
work that has no bead at the time of writing, so the bead is parked as blocked with a comment, to
be replaced by dependency edges when the categorisation work is written up.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The evaluation set holds at least 300 transactions whose budget line the user confirmed or
      corrected, spanning at least 3 calendar months, with every CPF removed. The report states
      its size and month span.
- [ ] At least 3 models running on the user's own hardware are measured, at no fewer than 2
      different sizes, beside the outside model in use on that day as the baseline. The report
      names each one with the exact version or tag that was run.
- [ ] Every arm receives the request the nightly job builds, byte for byte except the base URL
      and the model name. The report states this, or lists each difference a model required.
- [ ] For each arm the report gives four figures over the whole set: the share of rows whose
      budget line matches the user's; the share of rows answered at or above the auto-apply
      threshold in force (coverage); the share of matches among those rows; and the share of
      answers that were not valid against the response schema.
- [ ] For each local arm the report records the host's CPU, memory and GPU, and the peak memory
      the model used.
- [ ] Seconds per nightly batch, median of three runs per arm with the arms interleaved, are
      measured **by the review** rather than by whoever implements this, and recorded in the
      report.
- [ ] No file under version control contains a transaction description, a counterpart name or a
      per-row amount from the evaluation set: `git grep` for three descriptions sampled from the
      set returns nothing.
- [ ] The report ends with exactly one recommendation (switch, keep, or route by confidence) and
      the two figures it rests on.
- [ ] Done when: the report is committed at `docs/evaluations/local-models.md` and a reader can
      tell from it alone, without rerunning anything, which local model did best and by how many
      percentage points it trails or beats the baseline at the threshold in force.

## Tests
- Unit: the scoring functions (match share, coverage, match share above the threshold, invalid
  answer share) over a synthetic labelled fixture with known expected values, including a row
  with an invalid answer and a row exactly at the threshold.
- Unit: the loader refuses a set that still carries a CPF-shaped value.
- Manual check: the three measured runs per arm, standing in for an end-to-end test that cannot
  run in CI because the models and the labelled set exist only on the user's machines.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `tools/model-eval/`, `docs/evaluations/local-models.md`
**Reads only:** the backend code that builds the nightly categorisation request

A new, self-contained tool directory (the script, its scoring module and their tests) and one
report. Nothing in the backend or the interface changes; the request builder is read so the tool
sends the same request, and is not edited. If the comparison argues for switching, the switch
itself is a configuration change and belongs to a separate bead.

comments.text: Blocked on work that has no bead yet: the nightly categorisation job whose request this evaluation must reuse, and a few hundred categorisations confirmed or corrected by the user. When that work is written up as beads, replace this status with dependency edges (br dep add finwise-g82 <bead>) and set the status back to open.
